# Rajat Malik

> Rajat Malik is a senior lead software engineer and frontend architect based in
> Gurgaon, India. He leads frontend delivery at Siemens and has spent more than
> 15 years building enterprise web products across energy, mobility, parcel and
> telecom domains. He is an Angular and React specialist, the creator of 30+
> open-source libraries, extensions and developer tools, and a technical writer
> of 150+ articles.

Canonical page: https://rajatmalik.dev/
Contact: contact@rajatmalik.dev
Articles: https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/
RSS: https://rajatmalik.dev/feed.xml
Last updated: 2026-11-17

## Key facts

- **Current role:** Senior Lead Software Engineer at Siemens.
- **Experience:** 15+ years in software delivery, including 6+ years in energy
  automation. Previously Siemens Energy and HCL.
- **Specialisms:** Angular, React, TypeScript, micro-frontends, design systems,
  web performance, accessibility.
- **Open source:** 30+ published libraries and tools, including Angular
  components, PDF tooling, a JavaScript sandbox, a VS Code extension and Chrome
  extensions.
- **Writing:** 150+ technical articles on Medium, DEV Community, Hashnode and
  Substack, plus original in-depth articles on this site.
- **Talks and recognition:** technical talks, and recognition at Product Jam 2025
  for AI-powered prototyping.
- **Availability:** open to senior or lead frontend roles.
- **Location:** Gurgaon, Haryana, India.

## Original articles on this site

All six are original, long-form articles written for rajatmalik.dev. Each one
states the problem, the approach, the trade-offs and how to verify the result.

- **The Angular performance checklist I run before every release** — budgets,
  field data, change detection, lazy loading, `@defer`, images, runtime leaks
  and regression guards.
  https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/angular-performance-checklist.html
- **Where micro-frontend boundaries should actually go** — ownership-based
  splitting, the shell contract, shared-state discipline, versioned contracts
  and the independent-deploy test.
  https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/micro-frontend-boundaries.html
- **Core Web Vitals in 2026: the order of operations that moves the needle** —
  LCP, INP and CLS, field versus lab data, and the sequence that avoids
  optimising the wrong metric.
  https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/core-web-vitals-order-of-operations.html
- **Design systems that survive: tokens, contracts and honest review** —
  semantic tokens, composition-based component APIs, accessibility ownership,
  versioning and adoption metrics.
  https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/design-systems-that-survive.html
- **AI-assisted frontend development without lowering the bar** — where LLMs
  help, failure modes such as hallucinated APIs and phantom dependencies, and
  the review, testing and security gates that keep quality intact.
  https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/ai-assisted-frontend-development.html
- **A WCAG 2.2 checklist for component libraries** — the component-level
  accessibility contract, the criteria added in WCAG 2.2, and testing beyond
  automated scans.
  https://rajatmalik.dev/articles/wcag-2-2-component-checklist.html

## Editorial standards

Articles are written by Rajat Malik and reviewed before publication. They are
original to this site, not scraped or auto-generated summaries, and are not
sponsored. Corrections are accepted at contact@rajatmalik.dev and noted on the
affected page. Advertising is served by Google AdSense on content pages only;
the contact and legal pages are ad-free, and ads are kept separate from
editorial content. See the terms of use for the advertising disclosure.

## Selected projects

- **DeepWork** - a free, local-first focus timer and task manager for desktop and
  browser: https://deepwork.rajatmalik.dev/
- **DailyMilk** - a dairy operations dashboard for milk delivery logistics and
  stock management, built with Angular signals:
  https://dailymilk.rajatmalik.dev/
- **TracePulse** - framework-agnostic request monitoring and performance
  observability.
- **rm-ng-editor**, **rm-ng-typeahead**, **rm-ng-dynamic-layout**,
  **rm-ng-pdf-viewer**, **rm-ng-export-to-csv** and other Angular libraries,
  published on npm under the `@codewithrajat` and `rm-` scopes.
- **readLoude** - a Chrome extension that reads a page aloud with word-by-word
  highlighting.
- **dead-css-cleaner** - a VS Code extension that finds and removes unused CSS.
